name: Environmental regulation and monitoring
one_line: The regulator's own side of controlling environmental impact at named sites: a permit whose numbered conditions create obligations, and the open-ended stream of recurring monitoring returns, accredited sample analyses, inspection assessments, pollution incidents, and enforcement notices that those conditions generate. It differs from the government schema default in that its centre of gravity is not a decision lifecycle that terminates, but a perpetual measured-return stream keyed to a permit reference and a sampling point; its recognition therefore turns on determinand-with-unit-against-permitted-limit structure, sampling-point and facility identifiers, and chain-of-custody blocks, none of which appear in the schema's default signals. It declares no fields and no dimensions under PR-6.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every signal below inherits the government schema's holder-role precondition. The corpus holder or producer must be evidenced as the regulating authority. A named environment agency, a permit number, or environmental vocabulary never activates this row on its own, and no signal here licenses a government fact, because the schema declares no field rows.

a measured-return structure in which a determinand or parameter name, a numeric result, a unit of measurement, and a permitted limit or condition threshold occur as adjacent labelled slots or columns, repeated over dated rows, together with a permit or authorisation reference and a sampling point, outfall, borehole, or stack identifier

a recurring return keyed to a stated reporting period (a named quarter, month, or year) whose header repeats the same permit or authorisation reference across successive periods, and whose receipt is recorded on the authority side by a submission, logging, or return-register slot rather than by the operator's own covering letter alone

an authorisation instrument whose body is a numbered condition schedule — condition identifiers, an emission-limit or discharge-limit table, monitoring and reporting requirements, and an improvement or pre-operational condition list — issued under an issuing-authority block with an authorized-officer signature

an authority-side site assessment or inspection record with labelled operator, site, permit reference, condition-assessed, observation, and officer slots, where the compliance wording present in the document is retained as a literal source observation and never re-derived as a product conclusion

an accredited analytical report carrying a laboratory job or certificate reference, sample identifiers, a matrix or medium slot, an analyte list with method and reporting or detection limits, an accreditation-body block, and a signed chain-of-custody section naming sampler, transfer times, and receipt condition

a continuous or telemetered monitoring export whose rows are timestamped instrument readings with a channel or parameter name, an engineering unit, and validity, calibration, drift, or downtime flags, tied to a named stack, outfall, abstraction point, or ambient station under an authority-side collection system

a pollutant release or transfer inventory submission with a facility identifier, a pollutant or waste code list, a released or transferred quantity, and a receiving-medium slot (air, water, land, or off-site transfer), received under a stated collection round

an incident record with a notification timestamp, a substance or emission description, an affected receptor slot (watercourse, air, land, groundwater, habitat), an initial-response or containment log, and an authority incident reference distinct from the permit reference

a statutory enforcement or regulatory-action instrument — a notice reciting the condition or provision engaged, the steps required, a compliance date, appeal or representation rights, and an authorized-officer block — held by the issuing authority rather than by its recipient

an environmental complaint or reported-nuisance casework record with a complaint reference, a reported effect (odour, dust, noise, smoke, discharge), a location, and complainant contact slots, held in an authority case system

an authority regulated-site export or archive manifest whose member paths repeatedly encode one permit, site, or facility reference across permit, return, sample, inspection, incident, and enforcement families; the manifest is read without unpacking
needs_llm: deciding which side of the regulatory relationship holds the bytes when a monitoring return, sample result, permit copy, or inspection report is identical whether it sits in the regulator's case system or in the operator's compliance folder; interpretation may use only a bounded local dossier and must abstain when custody is unresolved

separating an authority acting as environmental regulator from the same authority acting as landowner, developer, operator of its own regulated assets, planning decision-maker, or public-health service — one municipality can appear in all of these roles across one corpus

separating a statutory environmental authorisation from a voluntary or contractual environmental scheme (a management-system certificate, a corporate sustainability disclosure, an eco-label, a supplier questionnaire) when both carry limits, audits, and numeric returns

recognizing an unlabelled officer file note, site visit memo, technical assessment, or condition-drafting note as authority-side work when it carries no letterhead and names only a site and a substance
reading OCR of a scanned monitoring sheet, hand-completed sampling form, or portal receipt to recover the permit reference and sampling point, while abstaining when the recovered tokens are ambiguous

judging whether a lab report, dataset, or inspection record has been supplied as environmental evidence to a different workflow — a legal matter, a property transaction, a research project, an insurance claim — in which case that workflow's own evidence governs and this row must not claim the file
never_alone: an environment agency, environmental protection body, water regulator, waste authority, or municipal environmental-health office name, seal, letterhead, or email domain alone; the body may be issuer, counterparty, cited authority, employer, data publisher, or the recipient of someone else's submission

environmental vocabulary alone — emissions, discharge, effluent, pollutant, contamination, sustainability, carbon, waste, hazardous, remediation, biodiversity — including a whole document written in it

a permit-shaped, licence-shaped, or facility-shaped identifier token alone; the same token appears on an operator's copy, a consultant's report, an objector's letter, a news download, and a published register extract

a determinand or chemical name with a unit alone (for example a nitrate value in milligrams per litre); the same pair appears in a research dataset, a bottled-water label, a school exercise, a health record, and a product specification
an operator, facility, or site name alone, and a parent folder named Environment, Environmental, EHS, Permits, Compliance, Monitoring, or Emissions alone

an authority-issued environmental permit, licence, exemption, registration, abatement notice, or waste transfer note held by the regulated party; that is the operator's compliance record, not authority-side custody
an ISO 14001, EMAS, or equivalent management-system certificate, audit report, or nonconformity log; conformity to a voluntary standard is not a statutory authorisation, whoever holds it

a published monitoring dataset, bathing-water result, air-quality index, state-of-the-environment report, or public register extract downloaded for reference; publication by a regulator is not authority-side custody
a corporate sustainability, ESG, carbon-disclosure, or scope-emissions report addressed to a regulator or investor; counterparty value does not activate this row
an environmental campaign, objection letter, petition, or consultation response written by a charity, community group, or individual, even when it quotes permit conditions verbatim
a file extension or source_type alone; the design says to "treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning"

a shared download session or browser batch that pulled a permit, a dataset, and a news article together; "A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact."

missing EXIF or dense OCR as proof that a site photograph is a portal screenshot rather than a camera image; "However, the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot."

work_types: permit, authorisation, consent, exemption, or registration determination with a numbered condition schedule, and its later variation, transfer, surrender, suspension, or revocation
periodic monitoring or compliance return received from a regulated site and logged against a permit condition
sampling visit record, field sheet, and chain-of-custody documentation
accredited laboratory analytical report and its result-versus-limit assessment
continuous or telemetered instrument data export and its calibration, validity, and downtime record
pollutant release, transfer, or waste-movement inventory submission for a collection round
site inspection or compliance assessment record and officer site note
pollution incident notification, response log, and post-incident review
environmental complaint or reported-nuisance casework held by the authority
regulatory-action or enforcement instrument, undertaking, remediation requirement, and prosecution-referral file
operator-submitted supporting technical material assessed by the authority — risk assessment, modelling, management plan, monitoring plan, closure or aftercare plan
public-register publication copy and redaction record for an environmental authorisation or return
grouping_reasons: one regulated site or installation, linked by an exact permit, authorisation, or facility reference repeated across the permit, its returns, sample results, inspections, incidents, and enforcement instruments; the group is open-ended and has no terminal event, unlike a decision lifecycle
one reporting period of one site, linking a return, its underlying sample reports, instrument exports, and any receipt or query correspondence through an exact period and permit reference
one sampling event, linking a field sheet, its chain-of-custody form, the laboratory certificate, and any site photograph carrying the same sample or point identifier

one incident, linking notification, response log, sample results taken in response, officer notes, and any resulting enforcement instrument through an exact incident reference distinct from the permit reference
one enforcement chain, linking the notice, its evidence bundle, representations received, and the compliance or appeal outcome

duplicate and version families remain universal relationships; a consolidated permit reissued after variation does not acquire new facts from its neighbourhood, and a superseded condition schedule is a version, not a new site
a complaint case joins a site group only through an exact permit, facility, or address anchor, and complainant identity never propagates to any other member

no group is a valid outcome for a standalone permit copy, notice, or published register extract; "Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group."

template.why: Empty by contract. PR-6 leaves the government schema fieldless, and a template cannot branch on undeclared fields, so no destination-eligible dimension exists to order. The world's real structure is stated as prose only: the regulated site or installation would organize first, because a monitoring return, a sample certificate, an inspection note, and an enforcement notice are all unintelligible detached from the site and permit they attest to; a bounded proceeding or incident reference would come next; work type would come last. Time is deliberately not first even though this row is the most time-dense situation on the government schema — the returns are periodic and the instrument exports are timestamped — because "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." A year-first tree would split one site's continuous record across every calendar folder and destroy the only comparison the world exists to support, which is one point measured against one limit over time. A period level is plausible as a second or third dimension once a site anchor exists, and any recommendation stays editable because "The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions." A complainant, operator contact, or officer must never become an organizing dimension.

collides_with.signal: Both hold an authority-issued authorisation with numbered conditions, an application file, and a determination. The permit-licensing row owns the lifecycle that terminates at grant, refusal, or renewal for any licensable activity. This row owns what the granted conditions then generate — recurring measured returns, sample analyses, and condition-referenced inspections. The competing fixture is one permit case folder: `Permit EPR-AB1234 - Consolidated Variation V3 - Schedule 3 Emission Limits.pdf` sits with permit-licensing when the evidence around it is application, assessment, and determination; it sits here when the evidence around it is a stream of returns and sample certificates keyed to its condition identifiers.

Both hold environmental assessment, modelling, monitoring proposals, and condition discharge for a named site. The planning row owns land-use consent and the material submitted to obtain it; this row owns operating control after an environmental authorisation exists. The competing fixture is `Environmental Statement - Mill Lane redevelopment - Chapter 8 Air Quality.pdf`: a planning application reference and a prospective mitigation frame place it with planning, while an environmental permit reference and assessment against an existing numbered condition place it here.

The reciprocal same-bytes case. An operator's compliance folder and a regulator's site file contain the identical permit copy, the identical monitoring return, and the identical laboratory certificate. This row requires authority-side custody — a return-register or receipt slot, an officer assessment, an issued instrument, or an authority case-system export. The manufacturing row owns the same bytes when the evidence shows the operator preparing, holding, or submitting them. The competing fixture is `EPR-AB1234 - Quarterly Monitoring Return Q2 2026 - Outfall 001.xlsx`: the operator's copy with a covering submission is manufacturing's, the copy carrying a date-received and receiving-officer slot is this row's, and when neither is present the file goes to Review Later rather than to a guess.

Both hold sampling programmes, laboratory results, premises inspections, and nuisance complaints, and one municipal office often runs both. This row requires an environmental authorisation, release, or receiving-medium frame — a permit condition, an emission or discharge point, a pollutant inventory. The public-health row owns population-health surveillance, disease and food-borne investigation, and health-protection casework. The competing fixture is `Complaint 26-4471 - odour - Mill Lane - caller details.docx`: a complaint traced to a permitted installation's abatement conditions is this row's, while the same complaint pursued as a health-protection investigation of exposed persons is public health's.

falls_through_to.when: a readable standalone permit copy, notice, certificate, return, or published register extract has durable value but no authority-side workflow and no accepted site group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: a complaint carrying complainant identity, a pre-enforcement investigation file, a prosecution referral, or a named-person incident record has no safe accepted group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a published environmental dataset, state-of-the-environment report, guidance note, or regulatory news item is held for reading rather than as authority-side work
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: the file is plainly environmental-regulatory in shape but the holder role is unresolved — an unattributed monitoring spreadsheet, a bare instrument export, a management-system audit with no authority marker
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: a monitoring database, an encrypted site-file export, a proprietary instrument binary, or a damaged submission cannot yield evidence beyond metadata
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.when: a positively evidenced screen capture of a returns portal, register page, or telemetry dashboard yields no accepted site or permit group through OCR
falls_through_to.design_cite: Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.

sensitivity_why: This row's posture is split rather than uniformly protective, and that split is one of the reasons it is not the schema default. Much of the corpus is destined for a statutory public register: permits, condition schedules, and many returns are published by design, and treating them as secrets would be wrong about the world. But the same site reference also gathers complainant names and addresses, whistleblower reports, pre-enforcement investigation material, prosecution referrals, commercially confidential process detail excluded from the register, and incident records naming individuals. The governing rule for this row is therefore that publication of one member never lowers the posture of the packet that shares its permit reference. The design requires: "Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector." Complainant identity in particular must not appear in a branch label, a group summary, or a model prompt, which is why a complainant is excluded from any dimension recommendation. The enum offers only none and potentially_sensitive; potentially_sensitive is the only safe value for a mixed packet.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: three items. (1) PR-6 leaves the government schema fieldless, so this row can describe a site-and-permit organizing structure but cannot serialize one; if PR-6 is lifted, adjudicate centrally whether a bounded authorisation reference, a regulated site or installation concept, a reporting period, and an environmental medium may exist as government fields, and which if any are destination-eligible — this row proposes none. (2) Decide the public-register question as policy rather than per row: whether a member that is provably on a statutory public register may be treated differently from its packet, or whether packet posture always dominates. (3) Decide whether the operator side and the regulator side of the identical monitoring return are resolved by evidence alone or by a user-declared corpus role; without a declared role, a large share of real corpora will legitimately route to Review Later.
